description: Single source of truth for all numeric quality gates (anti-AI scoring, self-review, rewrite limits, paragraph/unit word bounds, style-fingerprint compliance, voice rule-coverage/corpus minimums, typography). Edit here; every skill and agent references this file. Gemini model/thinking-budget defaults and retry policy are NOT read from here — they live in SPEC_DEFAULTS in plugins/academic-writer/mcp/gemini-server/src/gemini-client.ts (overridable per-project via profile.md), and the retry constants are hardcoded in that same file.

antiAi._comment: Paragraphs scoring below 35/50 trigger revision. 5 dimensions x 10 points each.

selfReview._comment: Articles scoring below 40/60 trigger researcher review before final output. 6 dimensions x 10 points each.

rewriteCycles._comment: Maximum number of times a paragraph can be rewritten before being included with [NEEDS REVIEW].

paragraph._comment: Soft word ceiling per paragraph. Introduction and conclusion paragraphs may exceed by wordCeilingIntroConclusionBonus words.

writerUnit._comment: Min/target/max word bounds for a 'writer unit' — the leaf-level chunk that gets exactly one section-writer subagent. Sections whose word count exceeds maxWords must be decomposed by the architect into multiple writer-unit subsections (an outline `units` array); adjacent subsections under minWords should be merged into one unit rather than left tiny.

styleFingerprint._comment: Per-dimension style compliance score. Below 7 triggers paragraph adjustment.

proofread._comment: Proofread pipeline caps, enforced in src/workflows/proofread.js from args.thresholds (WRK-14). chunkWords bounds one finder chunk; the mechanical loop exits 'converged' after dryRounds consecutive rounds with no fresh change, or 'cap-reached' at maxPasses. refuteVotes lenses verify each candidate change and refuteMajority of them refuting drops it.

typography._comment: dashReplacement is the default em/en-dash fix convention used by detect-ai-typography.py (values: hyphen|comma|colon|remove); overridable via --dash-replacement. topFrequentTermsCount/minTermLength configure extract-style-metrics.py's frequentTerms extraction. frontMatterParagraphs/frontMatterDocRatio/frontMatterShare drop title-page boilerplate from frequentTerms: a term counts as boilerplate when it appears in the first frontMatterParagraphs paragraphs of at least frontMatterDocRatio of the corpus files AND at least frontMatterShare of its total occurrences come from that front matter. Measured case: on a 10-file corpus the author's own first and last name ranked at 80 hits each and the assignment header מטלה at 74, all from title pages, and frequentTerms steers the write skill's vocabulary.
